questions.subject: science
questions.question: Which statement defines heat?
options: Energy transmitted due to difference in average kinetic energy of molecules
Sum of kinetic energy and positional energy of molecules
questions.explanation: Heat is energy transferred because of temperature difference. It flows from hotter body to colder body.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: When an object is heated, which change explains increase in volume?
options: Kinetic energy decreases, attraction increases and distance decreases
Kinetic energy remains zero and distance decreases
Attraction increases and distance becomes zero
Kinetic energy increases, attraction decreases and distance between molecules increases
questions.explanation: Heating makes molecules move faster. They move farther apart, so volume increases.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Specific heat capacity of a substance depends on which of the following?
questions.explanation: Specific heat capacity depends on the nature of substance. Different substances need different heat.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: What is an effect of the high specific heat capacity of water?
options: Water in the sea heats faster than land during the day
Water in the sea cools faster than land at night
Land cools faster than sea at night
Land heats slower than sea in the daytime
questions.explanation: Water heats and cools slowly. So land cools faster than sea at night.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Which is the best way to insert a wide pipe into a narrower pipe?
options: Heat the wider pipe and cool the narrow one
Cool the wider pipe and heat the narrow pipe
questions.explanation: Heating expands the wider pipe. Cooling contracts the narrow pipe, so fitting becomes easier.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: What are the lower fixed points of Celsius, Fahrenheit and Kelvin scales respectively?
questions.explanation: Lower fixed point is the freezing point of water. It is 0°C, 32°F and 273K.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: What is thermal energy?
options: Only the colour of a hot body
Only the volume of a gas
Total energy of molecules of a body
questions.explanation: Thermal energy is the total energy of molecules. More mass can mean more thermal energy.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: What is temperature?
options: Degree of hotness or coldness of a body
questions.explanation: Temperature tells how hot or cold a body is. It is degree of hotness or coldness.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: In which direction does heat flow naturally?
options: From higher temperature to lower temperature
From lower temperature to higher temperature only
From smaller body to larger body always
From lighter object to heavier object always
questions.explanation: Heat naturally flows from hot body to cold body. It flows until both reach the same temperature.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: What is thermal equilibrium?
options: Condition when bodies in contact reach the same temperature
questions.explanation: Thermal equilibrium means same temperature. Then net heat flow stops.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: What is one effect of heat on volume?
questions.explanation: Most substances expand when heated. Their volume increases.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: What is anomalous expansion of water?
options: Unusual expansion of water when cooled from 4°C to 0°C
questions.explanation: Water behaves unusually between 0°C and 4°C. It expands when cooled from 4°C to 0°C.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: At what temperature is water densest according to anomalous expansion?
questions.explanation: Water has maximum density at 4°C. At this temperature, its volume is least.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Why do water pipes crack in cold places in winter?
questions.explanation: Water expands when it freezes. This expansion can crack water pipes.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: What is specific heat capacity?
options: Heat required to melt all ice only
Heat required to raise temperature of 1 kg of substance by 1°C
questions.explanation: Specific heat capacity is heat needed for 1 kg substance to rise by 1°C. It shows how much heat a substance stores.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: What is the SI unit of specific heat capacity?
questions.explanation: The unit is joule per kilogram per degree Celsius. It is written as J/kg°C.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: What is the heat equation?
questions.explanation: Heat gained or lost is mass x specific heat x temperature change. So the formula is Q = msdt.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Why is water used in a car radiator?
options: It has high specific heat capacity and absorbs much heat
questions.explanation: Water has high specific heat capacity. It absorbs much heat without quick temperature rise.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Why is a hot water bag useful for hot pressure?
options: Water retains heat for a longer time due to high specific heat capacity
questions.explanation: Water stores heat for a long time. So a hot water bag remains warm longer.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Why is the temperature difference between day and night small in coastal areas?
options: Land has higher specific heat than water
Sea water heats and cools slowly
There is no heat transfer near sea
questions.explanation: Sea water heats and cools slowly. So coastal areas have small day-night temperature difference.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Why does an iron bar heat up when hammered continuously?
questions.explanation: Hammering does work on the iron bar. This work changes into heat.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Why does tea in an open cup stop cooling after some time?
options: It reaches thermal equilibrium with surroundings
questions.explanation: Tea cools until it becomes equal to room temperature. This is thermal equilibrium.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Why is there a large day-night temperature difference in deserts?
options: Low water content gives low heat storage
Sand has very high specific heat like water
questions.explanation: Deserts have little water to store heat. So they heat and cool quickly.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Which change occurs when water is heated from 0°C to 4°C?
options: Its volume increases and density decreases
Its volume decreases and density increases
questions.explanation: From 0°C to 4°C, water contracts. So its volume decreases and density increases.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Which change occurs when water is heated from 4°C to 10°C?
options: Its volume increases like ordinary liquids
questions.explanation: Above 4°C, water behaves like normal liquid. It expands when heated.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: How does an aluminium box affect melting of ice compared with wood?
options: Ice melts faster in aluminium because it conducts heat better
Ice melts faster in wood because wood is a metal
questions.explanation: Aluminium conducts heat better than wood. So heat reaches ice faster and melts it faster.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Why can water boil below 100°C in some conditions?
options: Pressure has no effect on boiling
Boiling point decreases when pressure decreases
questions.explanation: Lower pressure lowers boiling point. So water can boil below 100°C.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Which device measures temperature using expansion of liquid?
questions.explanation: A liquid thermometer uses expansion of liquid. Mercury or alcohol rises when heated.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: What is thermometer calibration?
options: Marking fixed points and divisions on a thermometer scale
questions.explanation: Calibration means marking fixed points and divisions. It makes the thermometer scale usable.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: What are lower and upper fixed points based on?
options: Melting point of ice and boiling point of water
questions.explanation: Thermometer fixed points use ice point and steam point. These are melting ice and boiling water points.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Which thermometer can measure temperature without touching the object?
questions.explanation: Infrared thermometer detects infrared radiation. It can measure temperature without touching.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: If two objects of the same material have different masses, which needs more heat for the same temperature rise?
questions.explanation: Heat needed depends on mass. Larger mass needs more heat for the same temperature rise.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: If temperature change doubles while mass and substance remain same, what happens to heat required?
questions.explanation: Heat is directly proportional to temperature change. If temperature change doubles, heat required doubles.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Why does touching hot tea feel hot but ice feel cold?
options: Heat flows from ice to hand only
Heat flows from tea to hand and from hand to ice
questions.explanation: Hot tea gives heat to the hand. Ice takes heat from the hand, so it feels cold.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Which is correct about heat and temperature?
options: Temperature is measured in joule only
Heat is energy transfer; temperature is degree of hotness
Heat is measured in degree Celsius only
questions.explanation: Heat is energy transfer. Temperature only tells how hot or cold something is.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Which statement best explains expansion on heating?
options: Molecular kinetic energy increases and average separation increases
questions.explanation: Heating increases molecular kinetic energy. Molecules move farther apart, so expansion occurs.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Why does land heat faster than sea in daytime?
options: Land has lower specific heat capacity than water
questions.explanation: Land has lower specific heat capacity than water. So land heats faster in daytime.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: What happens to density when most substances expand on heating?
options: Density decreases if mass remains same
questions.explanation: When volume increases but mass is same, density decreases. Density = mass / volume.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: What is the relation between heat lost and heat gained in mixing water when no heat escapes?
options: Both heat lost and gained are zero
Heat lost by hot water equals heat gained by cold water
questions.explanation: If no heat escapes, heat lost equals heat gained. This is used in mixing problems.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Which factor does not directly appear in Q = msdt?
questions.explanation: Q = msdt uses mass, specific heat and temperature change. Pressure is not in this formula.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: A large tank of cold water can have more thermal energy than a small bucket of lukewarm water. Why?
options: Thermal energy depends on mass as well as temperature
Small bodies always have more energy
questions.explanation: Thermal energy depends on mass and temperature. So a large cold tank can have more total thermal energy.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Why does water at the bottom of a steel jug feel warmer in winter?
options: Warm water is always less dense and settles lower
Ice is densest at 0°C and settles lower
Water near 4°C is denser and settles lower
questions.explanation: Water at 4°C is densest. So it settles at the bottom in winter.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: How does freezing of water differ from freezing of ghee or honey?
options: Water expands on freezing but ghee and honey contract
questions.explanation: Water expands on freezing. Ghee and honey are ordinary liquids, so they contract on freezing.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: If 500 g water is heated from 15°C to 85°C, which equation should be used?
questions.explanation: For heating water, use Q = msdt. It calculates heat for temperature change.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Why is water more effective than many liquids for cooling engines?
options: It absorbs a large amount of heat per kg per °C
questions.explanation: Water absorbs large heat per kg per °C. So it is useful for cooling engines.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Which graph trend identifies anomalous expansion of water?
options: Volume decreases from 0°C to 4°C and then increases
questions.explanation: Water volume decreases from 0°C to 4°C, then increases. This shows anomalous expansion.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Why should hot water not be poured suddenly into thick glass?
options: Water contracts instantly at high temperature
Unequal expansion may crack the glass
questions.explanation: Thick glass heats unevenly if hot water is poured suddenly. Unequal expansion can crack it.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: A thermometer is calibrated between ice point and steam point. What is being established?
options: A scale using lower and upper fixed points
questions.explanation: Calibration sets lower and upper fixed points. These points make a temperature scale.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Which conclusion is correct if two substances receive equal heat but one shows smaller temperature rise?
options: It has higher specific heat capacity
questions.explanation: A substance with higher specific heat rises less in temperature. It needs more heat for the same rise.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: A student says heat and temperature are identical. Which correction is best?
options: Heat is measured only in degree Celsius
Heat is energy in transfer; temperature shows degree of hotness based on average molecular energy
Temperature is measured only in joule
Both have no relation to molecules
questions.explanation: Heat is energy in transfer. Temperature shows degree of hotness based on molecular energy.
